claim: Regular sessions start on the second Monday of January every year unless law sets another day
quote: commencing on the second Monday of January of each year, unless a different day shall have been appointed by law

claim: The governor may call extraordinary sessions
quote: in extraordinary sessions when convened by the governor

claim: Legislative leaders must call a special session on petition of 60% of each house
quote: a joint written petition of at least sixty percent of the membership of each house

claim: A bill not returned within five days (Sundays excepted) during session becomes law
quote: Any bill which shall not be returned by the governor to the legislature within five days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to him, shall become a law

claim: After adjournment the governor has ten days (Sundays excepted) to file a veto or the bill becomes law
quote: within ten days after such adjournment (Sundays excepted) or become a law

claim: Acts take effect July 1 or sixty days after the session ends, whichever is later, unless an emergency is declared
quote: No act shall take effect until July 1 of the year of the regular session or sixty (60) days from the end of the session at which the same shall have been passed, whichever date occurs last

claim: The constitution bars acts taking effect before sixty days after session end, except emergencies
quote: No act shall take effect until sixty days from the end of the session at which the same shall have been passed, except in case of emergency

claim: General elections for state and county offices are in November of even-numbered years
quote: held on the first Tuesday succeeding the first Monday of November in each even-numbered year

claim: County officers are chosen at the even-year general election
quote: there shall be chosen all congressional, state and county officers

claim: The partisan primary is the third Tuesday of May in even-numbered years
quote: Primary elections shall be held on the third Tuesday of May in each even-numbered year.

claim: No more than two election dates a year in any county: the third Tuesday in May and the November Tuesday
quote: there shall be no more than two (2) elections conducted in any county in any calendar year

claim: The two permitted dates are the third Tuesday in May and the Tuesday after the first Monday in November
quote: The third Tuesday in May of each year; and (b) The Tuesday following the first Monday in November of each year.

claim: A district that voted on another date before 2011 moved to the nearest permitted date
quote: shall establish as the election date for that political subdivision the date authorized in subsection (1) of this section that falls nearest the date on which elections were previously conducted

claim: Water districts are exempt from the two-date limit
quote: Water districts governed by chapter 6, title 42

claim: City initiative and referendum elections are in November of odd-numbered years
quote: A city initiative or referendum election shall be held on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November of odd-numbered years.

claim: City general elections are in November of odd-numbered years and choose mayors and council members
quote: the election held on the first Tuesday succeeding the first Monday in November in each odd-numbered year at which there shall be chosen all mayors and councilmen

claim: Each city holds its general election in November of odd-numbered years
quote: on the Tuesday following the first Monday of November in each odd-numbered year

claim: In cities under 100,000, an uncontested mayor or council race is not held and the candidate is declared elected
quote: No city with a population of less than one hundred thousand (100,000) shall hold a city election for an office if

claim: School trustees are elected in November of odd-numbered years
quote: The election of school district trustees including those in charter districts shall be on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November in odd-numbered years.

claim: Each trustee zone elects the candidate with the most votes in the zone
quote: In each trustee zone, the person receiving the greatest number of votes cast within his zone shall be declared

claim: Trustees serve four-year terms
quote: a school district trustee shall be elected for a term of four (4) years

claim: Elementary school district boards have three trustees and other districts five, with exceptions after boundary changes
quote: The board of trustees of each elementary school district shall consist of three (3) members, and the board of trustees of each other school district shall consist of five (5) members.

claim: Trustees must live in the trustee zone they represent
quote: a resident of the trustee zone from which nominated or appointed

claim: Trustee candidates file declarations signed by five zone electors
quote: bear the signature of not less than five (5) school district electors resident of the trustee zone

claim: The county clerk runs elections for every political subdivision, including special districts
quote: the county clerk shall administer all elections on behalf of any political subdivision

claim: All school district and highway district elections follow the uniform district election law
quote: All school district and highway district elections shall be conducted pursuant to the provisions of this chapter 14, title 34

claim: Irrigation districts and several water-related districts are exempt from the uniform district election law
quote: irrigation districts governed by title 43 , Idaho Code, are exempt from the provisions of this chapter

claim: District candidates are nominated by petitions, not party
quote: Candidates for election in any political subdivision shall be nominated by nominating petitions

claim: Highway district commissioners are elected on a nonpartisan ballot
quote: There shall be a single nonpartisan ballot for the election of highway district commissioners in each highway district.

claim: Highway district commissioner: the candidate with the most votes wins
quote: The candidate with the most votes shall be declared the successful candidate.

claim: Single countywide highway district candidates file with the county clerk like party candidates
quote: single countywide highway district office pursuant to section 40-1404A

claim: Primary ballots are separate for each party
quote: There shall be a separate primary election ballot for each political party upon which its ticket shall be printed

claim: A voter affiliated with a party may vote only in that party's primary
quote: an elector who has designated a party affiliation shall be allowed to vote only in the primary election of the political party for which such an elector is so registered

claim: A party may open its primary to unaffiliated voters or another party's members by notice the previous November
quote: no later than the last Tuesday in the November prior to a primary election, notify the secretary of state in writing that the political party elects to allow

claim: An unaffiliated voter choosing a party's primary declares it at the polls and the choice is recorded in voting history
quote: The county clerk shall record such choice as part of the elector

claim: Party candidates must be affiliated with the party when they file
quote: All political party candidates shall declare their party affiliation in their declaration of candidacy and shall be affiliated with a party at the time of filing.

claim: County office candidates file party declarations with the county clerk before the primary
quote: Each political party candidate for county office

claim: A party candidate who loses the primary may not run in the general under another party or as an independent
quote: shall not be allowed to appear on the general election ballot under any other political party name or as an independent candidate

claim: The primary winner for a county office is the candidate with the most votes
quote: the political party candidates of each party who receive the highest number of votes for their particular county office

claim: County candidates with the most votes in November are elected
quote: the county candidates who received the highest number of votes for that particular office

claim: City candidates are nominated by declaration with no mention of party
quote: There shall be no mention relating to party or principal of the nominee.

claim: City races are won by the most votes; multi-seat races by the top vote-getters
quote: the candidate with the highest number of votes shall be declared elected

claim: Independents may not run in the primary
quote: No person may offer himself as an independent candidate at the primary election.

claim: An independent for county office files a declaration with a petition and declares no party affiliation
quote: must declare that he has no political party affiliation

claim: Idaho's counties are those of the territory as recognized at statehood
quote: The several counties of the territory of Idaho, as they now exist, are hereby recognized as legal subdivisions of this state.

claim: County government must be uniform throughout the state
quote: a system of county governments which shall be uniform throughout the state

claim: Every county commission has three members
quote: The board of county commissioners shall consist of three members.

claim: Each county must have a three-member board of commissioners
quote: Each county must have a board of county commissioners consisting of three (3) members.

claim: At each biennial election one commissioner is elected for two years and one for four years, rotating by district
quote: at each biennial election thereafter, one member shall be elected for a term of two (2) years and one for a term of four (4) years

claim: Counties have three commissioner districts
quote: must district their county into three (3) districts, as nearly equal in population as may be

claim: A commissioner must have lived in the district they represent for 90 days before the primary
quote: in the district which he represents for a period of ninety (90) days next preceding the primary election

claim: Counties elect a sheriff, assessor, coroner and treasurer every four years
quote: for the election of a sheriff, a county assessor, a county coroner and a county treasurer, who is ex-officio public administrator, every four years

claim: The clerk of the district court is ex officio auditor and recorder
quote: The clerk of the district court shall be ex-officio auditor and recorder.

claim: No other county offices may be established
quote: No other county offices shall be established

claim: The statutory list of county officers
quote: The officers of a county are: 1. A sheriff. 2. A clerk of the district court, who shall be ex officio auditor and recorder, and ex officio clerk of the board of county commissioners. 3. An assessor. 4. A prosecuting attorney.

claim: A prosecuting attorney is elected every four years in every county
quote: every four (4) years thereafter, a prosecuting attorney shall be elected in every county

claim: A clerk of the district court is elected every four years in every county
quote: every four (4) years thereafter, a clerk of the district court shall be elected in every county

claim: Counties and cities may make local police, sanitary and other regulations not in conflict with general law
quote: may make and enforce, within its limits, all such local police, sanitary and other regulations as are not in conflict with its charter or with the general laws

claim: Cities are organized and classified by general law
quote: The legislature shall provide by general laws for the incorporation, organization and classification of the cities and towns

claim: An area with at least 125 qualified electors may petition to incorporate as a city
quote: containing not less than 125 qualified electors

claim: City council has four or six members, half elected at each general city election (except council-manager cities)
quote: a council consisting of either four (4) or six (6) members, one half (1/2) of whom shall be elected at each general city election

claim: Council members serve four-year terms
quote: shall hold office for a term of four (4) years

claim: The mayor serves a four-year term
quote: The term of office of mayor shall be for a period of four (4) years except as otherwise specifically provided.

claim: Outside council-manager cities, the mayor is the chief administrative official and votes only to break ties
quote: have a vote only when the council is equally divided

claim: Any city may adopt the council-manager plan by vote
quote: may adopt the council-manager plan of government by proceedings as herein provided

claim: A city may change between four and six council members by election
quote: Any city may change to the greater or lesser number of councilmen after an election

claim: A city may number its council seats by ordinance
quote: Any city, by ordinance, may assign a number to each council seat.

claim: Cities under 100,000 may elect council by district; cities over 100,000 must
quote: Any city having more than one hundred thousand (100,000) inhabitants based upon the most recent federal decennial census shall establish districts and shall elect councilmen by districts

claim: Smaller cities may choose district elections by ordinance
quote: may, by ordinance, provide for districts and the election of councilmen by districts

claim: City elections in a city spanning counties are run jointly by the county clerks
quote: Elections in a city located in more than one (1) county shall be conducted jointly by the clerks of the respective counties

claim: Joint school districts crossing county lines have elections run jointly by the county clerks, coordinated by the home county
quote: Elections in a joint school district or other political subdivisions that extend beyond the boundaries of a single county shall be conducted jointly by the clerks of the respective counties
